overview.problemStatement: QuickBooks Online is the accounting system of record for most consumers, but wirekit has no QuickBooks module, so every integration re-implements OAuth2 token handling, realm-scoped routing, Intuit Fault parsing, and webhook verification, and mistakes produce duplicate invoices in a system of record.
overview.proposedSolution: Add a quickbooks feature-flagged module exposing QuickBooksClient, Customer, Invoice, Payment, Account, and Item per catalogue/13_quickbooks.md: create/update/read, invoice lines, void, send, payment recording, account and item listing, OAuth2 refresh-before-expiry, and intuit-signature webhook verification, reusing the crate client, retry, rate-limit, secret, and error types.
overview.targetAudience: Rust developers syncing accounting data, including an invoicing and accounting agent in a consuming application.
assumptions: Intuit app approval, sandbox credentials, and the realm id are [to be confirmed]; the module assumes approved OAuth2 credentials.
Base URL is https://quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3/company/{realmId} with a minorversion query parameter.
Access tokens live about 60 minutes; refresh tokens rotate and must be persisted by the caller.
No external research was performed beyond the repository catalogue and constitution (CON-704).
outOfScope: OAuth2 authorization-code browser flow and token persistence.
Payroll, tax filing, and other Intuit products.
Bulk or batch endpoints and CDC polling.
Accounting domain rules such as revenue recognition (CON-106).

userStories.title: Connect and refresh OAuth2 tokens
userStories.want: the module to manage the token lifecycle
userStories.benefit: sync jobs do not fail at expiry

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given client id, client secret, refresh token, and realm id, when the client is built, then credentials are held in Secret and Debug renders no plaintext.
Given an expired or soon-to-expire access token, when a request is made, then the module refreshes once, applies the token, and retries exactly once.
Given a refresh returning a new refresh token, when it succeeds, then the caller receives the rotated token, and a persistent 401 after one refresh fails instead of looping.

userStories.title: Sync customers
userStories.benefit: a customer created in the product exists in accounting

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a customer payload, when create is called, then a POST to the realm customer resource sends the display name and optional contact fields and returns the created entity with its id.
Given an existing customer id and changed fields, when update is called, then the request carries Id and SyncToken and returns the entity with an incremented sync token.

userStories.title: Create, read, void, and send invoices
userStories.benefit: completed work becomes a billable document

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a customer reference and at least one line, when create_invoice is called, then the request carries the customer reference and ordered lines with amount, description, and item reference.
Given an existing invoice, when void_invoice is called, then the request uses the documented void operation and the returned invoice reports a voided balance.
Given an existing invoice, when send_invoice is called, then the request targets the send operation and the response records the delivery.
Given an invoice id and an amount, when record_payment is called, then the payment references the invoice and the amount is expressed in the linked transaction.
Given a payment over the invoice balance, when it is recorded, then the caller receives a typed validation error rather than a silent partial success.

userStories.title: Read accounts and items
userStories.benefit: invoice lines point at real accounts and items

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a realm, when list_accounts or list_items is called, then the module returns typed entries with id and name using the query endpoint with a bounded result size.

userStories.title: Verify webhooks
userStories.benefit: only Intuit can trigger a resync

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given raw bytes, the verifier token, and a correct intuit-signature, when verification runs, then the HMAC comparison is constant time and returns the parsed notification.
Given a wrong or missing signature, when verification runs, then it fails closed and nothing is parsed; a repeated event id is reported as a duplicate.

userStories.title: Fail predictably
userStories.want: Intuit faults, retries, and duplicate protection handled consistently
userStories.benefit: sync failures never corrupt the accounting record

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an Intuit Fault with Error entries, when a call fails, then the error is WirekitError::Api exposing every Intuit code and message.
Given a 429 with Retry-After, when the call is retried, then the policy honours the header and validation faults are never retried.
Given a caller-supplied idempotency key, when a create is retried, then the module checks for an existing entity by that key before creating a duplicate.

functionalRequirements.text: The crate MUST expose an additive, default-off quickbooks feature that enables no other provider.
QuickBooksClient MUST hold credentials and refresh tokens in Secret, reject a non-HTTPS base URL, and read no environment variables.
The module MUST provide QuickBooksClient, Customer, Invoice, Payment, Account, and Item as named in the catalogue.
Token refresh MUST happen before expiry and at most once per request, surfacing the rotated refresh token.
Customer create and update MUST be supported, with Id and SyncToken on update.
Invoice create with ordered lines, void, and send MUST be supported.
Payments MUST reference an invoice and over-balance amounts MUST produce a typed error.
Account and item listing MUST use the query endpoint with a bounded result size.
Webhook verification MUST use HMAC over raw bytes with a constant-time comparison and MUST fail closed.
Duplicate webhook events MUST be detectable by event id.
Intuit Fault bodies MUST map to WirekitError::Api preserving every code and message.
Retries MUST honour Retry-After for 429 and 5xx, MUST NOT retry validation faults, and creates MUST support an idempotency check.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Client credentials, access and refresh tokens, and the webhook verifier token MUST be held in Secret and render redacted (CON-511, CON-519).
Every request MUST be realm-scoped by the configured realm id; a contradicting per-call realm MUST be rejected (CON-512).
Provider responses and webhook bodies MUST be size-bounded and typed before use (CON-515).
All traffic MUST use HTTPS and a cleartext base URL MUST be rejected at construction (CON-520).
The rotated refresh token MUST be surfaced so the caller can persist it, and losing it MUST NOT silently continue with a stale token.
The module MUST compile under forbid(unsafe_code) and deny(missing_docs) (CON-201, CON-202).

edgeCases.description: Refresh succeeds but the rotated refresh token is not persisted
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The next run fails authentication rather than reusing a stale token.

edgeCases.description: Two creates with the same idempotency key race
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The second finds the existing entity or surfaces the provider duplicate error.

edgeCases.description: Webhook replays the same event id
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Reported as a duplicate instead of resyncing twice.

edgeCases.description: Invoice line references a missing item in the realm
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Provider validation fault surfaced as a typed error naming the item.

risks.description: Intuit app approval, sandbox credentials, and a realm are unconfirmed.
risks.mitigation: Verify against a local mock of documented shapes as m5-gated-integrations did; keep the assumption marked [to be confirmed].

risks.description: Refresh-token rotation is lossy if the caller does not persist the new value.
risks.mitigation: NFR-005 plus an explicit result type carrying the rotated token.

risks.description: QuickBooks entity schemas change with minorversion.
risks.mitigation: One version constant, documented and asserted in tests.
